assumptions.impact: All geometry-derived areas and ratios are low-confidence submission measurements and must be recomputed from official georeferenced redlines before statutory or professional scoring use.
assumptions.statement: Repository provisional geometry is used because no official redline is available; it is not an official boundary or precise statutory area basis.

assumptions.impact: Development intensity remains unknown; conceptual values cannot be presented as approved planning controls.
assumptions.statement: Statutory controls, including FAR, height, density, setbacks, control lines, and approved land-use conditions, are missing.

assumptions.impact: Retain-renovate-demolish, capacity, displacement, and implementation claims remain conceptual pending survey and title review.
assumptions.statement: Existing building footprints, heights, uses, ages, condition, parcel boundaries, and ownership records are missing.

assumptions.impact: Mobility and infrastructure layers are organizational concepts, not engineering alignments or feasibility conclusions.
assumptions.statement: Official transport redlines, sections and operations data, and municipal, utility, fire, flood, heritage, and public-facility data are missing.

assumptions.impact: These layers communicate a proposal only and are not observed conditions, statutory controls, approvals, or construction documents.
assumptions.statement: Land use, building, road, green-space, public-space, and phasing layers are conceptual generated design layers clipped to provisional geometry.

assumptions.impact: No archive item may be collected, published, reused for AI, or retained beyond its consent scope; withdrawal must propagate to every governed copy and index.
assumptions.statement: The skill-archive requires granular consent for each contribution, separate visibility choices, revocable permissions, and an accessible withdrawal workflow.

assumptions.impact: Unlabeled or unversioned AI-derived content cannot enter the public archive or support an outcome claim.
assumptions.statement: AI-derived content requires clear labeling, provenance links, model and prompt-context versioning, edit history, and a visible distinction from resident-authored material.

assumptions.impact: Affected content or activity must pause safely, preserve an audit record, and route to an accountable trained reviewer before publication or action.
assumptions.statement: Activity safety requires human review for sensitive, contested, or higher-risk outputs, plus a documented failure-to-human path when automation is uncertain, unavailable, or challenged.

assumptions.impact: Outcome values remain unknown and may only be reported after consented, quality-checked pilot measurement with versioned definitions.
assumptions.statement: Pilot outcome metrics have no observed baseline; numerator, denominator, cohort, service window, sampling, consent, and exclusion rules must be fixed before collection.
